messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: P0 Routing anomaly detected - sudden cross-pool traffic from hosted -> dedicated pools in us-east-2. Error rate spike 12% across 3 tenants. Paging oncall @samir_oncall :rotating_light:
samir_oncall: on it. starting triage, tagging eng-sre. any obvious config churn in last 30m?
mike_eng: saw a spike in fallback events from smart-router: fallback->dedicated then fallback->hosted in a loop. logs show route decisions alternating for same request id.
anya_sre: initial thought: policy mis-eval — the new autoscaler label change may have exposed dedicated nodes as "available" to hosted routing. pulling routing-policy and pool labels now.
samir_oncall: @mike_eng can you paste the last 10 routing decisions for tenant acme-enterprise?
mike_eng: here are the condensed lines from router logs (sanitized):
```
[12:41:02] request=R-9a3 route=hosted->dedicated pool=dedicated-us-east-2-pool-42 reason=fallback_quota
[12:41:03] request=R-9a3 route=dedicated->hosted pool=dedicated-us-east-2-pool-42 reason=capacity_mismatch
[12:41:03] request=R-9a3 route=hosted->dedicated pool=dedicated-us-east-2-pool-42 reason=fallback_quota
```
samir_oncall: that's the loop. same request toggling. looks like the fallback policy has criteria that re-evaluates pool availability too quickly and the dedicated pool is considered both eligible and ineligible within milliseconds.
anya_sre: I pulled the routing policy config that rolled out ~20m ago (change-id: cfg-2026-03-15-688). snippet: 
```
route_policy:
  - match: { capacity_tier: "dedicated" }
    allow_hosted_fallback: true
    fallback_window_ms: 100
```
The problem: our autoscaler updated pool label to "capacity_tier: \"dedicated-ephemeral\"" and the match is doing a substring-like equality in the policy engine, causing a false-positive hit. so router treats dedicated pool as eligible for hosted fallback, then later health checks flip it.
mike_eng: confirm: autoscaler changed label during scale-in. dedicated pool briefly reported as available for hosted traffic because the label check matched incorrectly.
customer_ops: customer acme-enterprise reporting degraded responses and some requests returned model-variant "redwood-13b-qa" (dedicated) for hosted sessions. this is a major tenant isolation concern.
samir_oncall: ok mitigation plan: 1) block dedicated pools from accepting hosted routes via immediate policy override 2) increase fallback_window_ms to 5s to prevent flip-flop 3) roll back autoscaler label change or reconcile labels 4) engage SRE lead for postmortem
anya_sre: executing step 1: applying emergency override (console API)
```
curl -X POST https://internal.console/api/v1/route/overrides \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \
  -d '{"selector":"pool:detailed:dedicated-us-east-2-pool-42","allow_hosted":false,"ttl_s":600}'
```
deploy-bot: override applied to pool dedicated-us-east-2-pool-42 by anya_sre — change-id: ov-1865432100-1; propagation 2/3 regions
mike_eng: applying step 2: bumping fallback_window_ms to 5000 for smart-router service via feature-flag (ff-routing-fallback-window=5000). patch applied to canary routers.
deploy-bot: feature-flag update rolled to canary (router-canary-3). no errors.
anya_sre: step 3: triggering label reconcile job against autoscaler to restore exact label "capacity_tier: \"dedicated\"". running job: reconcile-autoscaler-1865432100.
anya_sre: also adding an explicit tenant_isolation check on router so hosted requests must match pool. config snippet applied to canary:
```
route_policy:
  - match: { capacity_tier: "dedicated" }
    tenant_isolation: true
    allow_hosted_fallback: false
```
sre_lead: good. we should also blackhole any in-flight requests showing mismatched tenant headers to prevent cross-tenant leakage. can we drop those responses?
mike_eng: yes we added a quick filter to router to verify tenant header against pool_tenant_tag; dropping mismatched responses and logging full context to incident trace index. patched canary.
customer_ops: ACME ticket updated: we've applied temporary routing isolation; they still see some errors for ~2 minutes after the override. asking for ETA to full remediation.
samir_oncall: estimated mitigation in progress — overrides + ff + reconcile should fully stop loops within 2-3 min, then we'll roll full change to all routers. telling customer ~15min for full propagation and post-checks.
deploy-bot: override propagation complete to all regions. feature-flag rolled to 100%. reconcile job returned: corrected labels on 3 nodes in pool.
anya_sre: monitoring: error rate dropping from 12% -> 1.4% over last 90s. no additional tenant cross-hits detected by our checks.
samir_oncall: handing off to @mike_eng for postmortem ownership. I'm going offline for followup tasks.
mike_eng: taking ownership of postmortem. immediate action items: (1) revert the loose label-match logic in policy engine (hotfix), (2) add unit tests for autoscaler->router label semantics, (3) run a one-week check to ensure no other pools have label variants, (4) update runbook for fallback_window defaults.
sre_lead: please file P0 postmortem with timeline, impact summary, and RCA. include customer comms draft for ACME.
customer_ops: ACME notified: temporary fix applied, we are performing full verification, will update within 30m.
samir_oncall: closing page for now — moving to incident tracking. thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
